# SB-1003: Safety bulletin: arc flash at the induction power cabinet

Revision: Rev A  
Plant: P2, line P2-L3  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L3-HT02

Hazard description
This bulletin addresses a recurring arc flash hazard observed at the induction power cabinet serving the heat treat line on P2-L3. Faults inside the cabinet have produced energetic electrical arcing during component failure and during maintenance access when the cabinet was assumed to be de-energized but residual or backfeed energy remained. Arc flash events have the potential to cause severe thermal injury, blast-related trauma, and ignition of surrounding materials. Contributing factors identified in recent inspections include degraded insulation at high-current conductors, loose connections at power distribution terminations, and inconsistent thermocouple signal integrity that has led to unexpected control behavior at the heat treat furnace. The work environment at the cabinet includes confined access, limited egress, and proximity to combustible oils and process wiring bundles, increasing the consequence of an arc event.

Affected equipment
This bulletin applies to the induction power cabinet and associated control and sensing equipment for Machining heat treat furnace #2. The thermocouple calibration interval for Machining heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L3-HT02) is 50 days. The scope includes the cabinet enclosure, main bus connections, control contactors and solid state devices, sensing harnesses routed into the cabinet, and the immediate work area that maintenance and electrical staff must access. Operations personnel who perform furnace starts or parameter changes and maintenance personnel who perform inspection, troubleshooting, or repair on the cabinet are included in the affected population.

Required controls
Controls are organized as administrative, engineering, and personal protective measures. These controls are mandatory for any personnel entering the cabinet work area for tasks that expose energized conductors or that involve opening the cabinet.

- Administrative controls
  - Implement a job briefing and documented risk assessment prior to any work at the cabinet. The briefing must identify potential arc flash sources, confirm isolation steps to be followed, and assign roles for an observer and a qualified person to conduct verification. Record the briefing outcome in the equipment maintenance log and attach to the work order.
  - Require use of the pre-work checklist from SOP-P2-L3-02 for all cabinet access activities. The checklist must be completed and signed by the assigned qualified person and retained with the maintenance record.
  - Schedule thermocouple calibration activities per the stated calibration interval to prevent sensor drift that can cause improper control actions leading to unexpected energization sequences.
  - Restrict access to authorized qualified personnel only. Non-qualified personnel are prohibited from opening or adjusting the cabinet.

- Engineering controls
  - Before any access, ensure full isolation of the cabinet supply per the isolation procedure in MM-P2-L3-HT02. Verify that isolation is complete and documented in the isolation log.
  - Use a tagout and lockout system consistent with MM-P2-L3-HT02-S3. Locks and tags must remain in place until verification tests confirm de-energized conditions and all work is complete.
  - Where practical, relocate frequently adjusted low-voltage controls to an external control panel or provide remote access to reduce the frequency of cabinet openings.
  - Replace or secure suspected degraded terminations and insulation identified during inspection. Any repairs that require energization for testing must follow a written plan that minimizes exposure and uses remote testing where available.

- Personal protective measures
  - Qualified personnel must use PPE appropriate for arc hazard exposures as defined by site procedures. Ensure PPE is inspected and maintained. Do not improvise or omit required clothing or face protection.
  - Establish and enforce a minimum clearance zone around the cabinet during energized testing. Only essential personnel are permitted inside the zone, and a safety observer must be positioned outside the immediate clearance area to communicate emergency stop commands.

Step rationale and examples
The requirement to adhere to the thermocouple calibration interval addresses a root cause of unexpected behavior in the control system. When thermocouples drift outside acceptable accuracy, the furnace control logic may initiate sequences that alter power demand or engage switching devices in a manner not anticipated by operators. Ensuring the thermocouple calibration interval for Machining heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L3-HT02) is 50 days reduces the probability of control-induced energization events that can precede an arc flash.

Example scenario: A drifted thermocouple signal caused a control controller to command a rapid power change while an operator was accessing the cabinet for an unrelated inspection. The unexpected command energized a section of the bus that had been assumed safe, producing an arc at a loose termination. Following the controls in this bulletin—pre-work checklist, isolation verification, and strict adherence to the calibration interval—would have interrupted the chain of events.

Records to keep
Maintain the following documentation in the equipment file and the plant electronic maintenance record system:
- Completed pre-work checklists and risk assessments from SOP-P2-L3-02 attached to the work order.
- Isolation verification tags and the isolation log entries as required by MM-P2-L3-HT02.
- Lockout/tagout records and any deviations documented under MM-P2-L3-HT02-S3.
- Thermocouple calibration certificates and calibration dates showing compliance with the thermocouple calibration interval for Machining heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L3-HT02) is 50 days.
- Repair and inspection reports for terminations, insulation condition, and any component replacements performed inside the cabinet.
- Incident reports for any arc flash or near-miss events including root cause analysis and corrective actions.

Effective date
Revision: Rev A

Related documents
- MM-P2-L3-HT02
- MM-P2-L3-HT02-S3
- SOP-P2-L3-02

Actions required by recipients
Review this bulletin, update local job plans and procedures to incorporate the controls described, and verify that maintenance and calibration schedules reflect the thermocouple calibration interval for Machining heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L3-HT02) is 50 days. Supervisors are to confirm completion of these actions and file the verification records in the equipment maintenance folder.
